pendingSeal.message: Certification of the boundary and topography by a Maryland licensed surveyor. The plan is complete and delivered; this is the review step that follows. The boundary shown is GIS, compiled rather than surveyed — in testing, county GIS was 4.3 ft off the surveyed line and a front setback flipped from compliant to non-compliant once corrected.

Quantify the unknown disturbance components (Building footprint, Driveway, Utility trenches, Grading, Stockpiles, Construction access, Offsite work, Demolition, Staging areas). Until then the 5,000 sq ft determination is not defensible either way, and it decides whether sediment control and stormwater management review apply.
Maryland surveyor-certified boundary and topographic survey (surveyor): GIS parcel geometry is preliminary and may be offset from surveyed boundaries. A permit submission needs certified geometry.
Confirm with DPS whether the disturbance requires a sediment control permit and a stormwater concept.
Confirm Forest Conservation Law applicability with M-NCPPC Montgomery Planning.

Recorded plat: Montgomery County Plat No. 143 (M-NCPPC 164-113), recorded 1911-09-07 (http://plats.msa.maryland.gov/pages/unit.aspx?cid=MO&qualifier=s&series=1249&unit=007953). The plat is the boundary of record; transcribe its calls — the county parcel drawn here is compiled GIS.

Zoning envelope — Chapter 59 standard method, reconciled 2026-09-25 through the enacted ZTAs. A lot recorded before 1958 may take the exemptions of ZTA 16-07 (§7.7), which is read by the reviewer. Height 35 ft to a flat roof; 30 ft to the mean of eaves and ridge of a pitched roof. Front setback may be increased by the Established Building Line, §4.4.1.A. Lots platted before 1978 and under 25,000 SF may have to satisfy Residential Infill Compatibility, §4.4.1.B.
Review and seal by the professionals responsible for each subject. The platform drafts a complete plan; the seal is a human act that follows delivery. Nothing here implies county approval.
